title: Rav Dimi bar Chinena (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was younger than Rava, and he had a brother named Ravin, as in Bava Batra 13b: Ravin bar Chinena and Rav Dimi bar Chinena — their father left them two maidservants … they came before Rava.

This Rav Dimi is mentioned in Eruvin 61a, disagreeing with Rav Safra; in Bava Kamma 98b he said, “This of Rabbah is a dispute of Rabbi Shimon,” etc., and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua objects to his statement; in Sanhedrin 84b he disagrees with Rav Mattenah and says: “Just as one who strikes an animal for healing is exempt, so one who strikes a person for healing is exempt.” His brother Ravin lived also in Rav Ashi’s time, as in Pesachim 109b.

notes.text: פריך means raising an objection, not necessarily successfully refuting the position. The first and second Rav Dimi entries are not merged, and the brothers’ father and chronological inference remain the supplied account.
Rav Dimi II remains distinct from Rav Dimi I; an objection by Rav Huna does not itself establish a successful refutation.
